title: [BUG] apm update repeatedly re-updates git-semver deps already at their locked tag
body:
**Describe the bug**

`apm update` (including `apm update -g`) reports a spurious **UPDATE on every run** for git-source semver dependencies that are already at their locked tag, and never converges. Re-running yields the same "N updated" line indefinitely; the lockfile is rewritten with the **identical** commit SHA each time — only `generated_at` / `resolved_at` timestamps change. No deployed files change on disk, so the effect is cosmetic but persistent and undermines trust in `apm update` output (you can't tell a real update from noise).

This is the git-source counterpart of the registry idempotency bug fixed in #1908 — that fix corrected the registry path but not git-semver deps.

**To Reproduce**

1. `apm.yml`:
   ```yaml
   name: repro
   version: 0.1.0
   targets: [claude]
   dependencies:
     apm:
       - owner/repo/packages/some-pkg#>=2.0.0 <3.0.0   # any git-source semver range
   ```
2. `apm install --target claude`
3. `apm update --yes --target claude` → `Updated N APM dependencies`
4. `apm update --yes --target claude` → `Updated N APM dependencies` (again)
5. …repeats forever. `git diff apm.lock.yaml` between two consecutive updates shows only `generated_at` / `resolved_at` timestamp lines — zero substantive change.

**Expected behavior**

After the first `apm update`, subsequent runs should report **"All dependencies already at their latest matching refs."** — as already happens for git deps pinned to concrete SHAs, and for registry deps since #1908.

**Environment (please complete the following information):**
 - OS: macOS
 - Python Version: 3.14.4
 - APM Version: 0.24.0 and 0.24.1 (reproduces on both; `install/plan.py` is byte-identical between them)
 - Also reproduces on both project-scope and `--global`, and on a fresh isolated project (not specific to any one layer).

**Root cause**

On `apm update`, the git-semver resolver (`_maybe_resolve_git_semver`, `install/phases/resolve.py`) rewrites `dep.reference` to the concrete tag and computes its SHA (`GitSemverResolution.resolved_sha`), but stashes the result in `ctx.git_semver_resolutions` / the download result **without attaching it back to `dep.resolved_reference`**.

`build_update_plan` (`install/pipeline.py`, invoked right after resolve and before download) reads `dep.resolved_reference`, which is `None` at that point, so `_extract_new_ref_and_commit` returns the correct concrete tag for the ref but `None` for the commit. The classifier then compares `old_commit` (real locked SHA) vs `new_commit` (`None`) and emits `update`, even though `old_ref == new_ref`.

Instrumented plan-time state:
```
PLAN-TIME DEP STATE
  key=.../packages/eli5 reference='eli5--v2.0.0' resolved_reference=None
PLAN ENTRIES
  update: ...eli5 old_commit='69148d93...' new_commit=None old_ref='eli5--v2.0.0' new_ref='eli5--v2.0.0'
```

**Proposed fix**

Mirror #1908's registry approach on the git-source path: in `build_update_plan`, when a dep has no freshly-resolved commit, the locked entry pins an immutable tag (`resolved_tag` set), and the ref is unchanged, borrow the locked commit so the comparison yields `unchanged`. Scoped to tags so branch-tip advances still surface as real updates.

I have a candidate patch with a failing-then-passing regression test plus a branch-tip guard (112 relevant tests green) and end-to-end verification that `apm update` converges after the first run. Happy to open a PR against `microsoft/apm` if the approach looks right — draft on my fork: https://github.com/srobroek/apm/pull/1

title: [BUG] Shared clone cache conflates nested GitLab repositories
body:
**Describe the bug**

`apm install` can reuse the wrong repository when two virtual subdirectory
dependencies live in different repositories under the same nested GitLab
namespace and use the same ref. The first clone wins the per-run shared clone
cache; later dependencies materialize from that unrelated bare clone and fail
with `Subdirectory '<path>' not found in repository`.

The cache currently derives `(owner, repo)` from only the first two components
of `DependencyReference.repo_url`. For example, both
`acme/platform/team/repo-a` and `acme/platform/team/repo-b` become
`(acme, platform)`.

**To Reproduce**

1. Create two GitLab repositories beneath the same nested namespace, each with
   a different APM package subdirectory.
2. Declare both as object-form dependencies at the same default ref:

   ```yaml
   dependencies:
     apm:
       - git: https://gitlab.com/acme/platform/team/repo-a.git
         path: packages/package-a
       - git: https://gitlab.com/acme/platform/team/repo-b.git
         path: packages/package-b
   ```

3. Run `apm install --verbose`.
4. Observe that one dependency installs and the other reports its valid
   subdirectory as missing. Reversing declaration/download order changes which
   repository succeeds.

**Expected behavior**

Repositories with distinct full Git identities must receive distinct shared
and persistent cache keys. Subdirectories from both repositories should be
materialized from their own upstream clones.

**Environment (please complete the following information):**

- OS: macOS 15 (arm64)
- Python Version: bundled standalone CLI
- APM Version: reproduced with 0.13.0 and 0.24.0; the same key construction is
  present on current `main` / 0.25.0 source
- VSCode Version: not relevant

**Logs**

Verbose output reports every nested repository against the same shortened
clone identity and then fails during subdirectory extraction:

```text
[i] perf: subdir gitlab.com/acme/platform/team/repo-b/packages/package-b
    cache=shared-bare sparse=packages/package-b
[x] Failed to install .../repo-b/packages/package-b:
    Subdirectory 'packages/package-b' not found in repository
```

**Additional context**

The collision originates in `GitHubPackageDownloader.download_subdirectory()`:

```python
cache_owner = dep_ref.repo_url.split("/")[0]
cache_repo = dep_ref.repo_url.split("/")[1]
```

The persistent cache canonical URL repeats the same truncation. A regression
test should use two repository identities that share their first namespace
segments and assert that the clone/materialization cache does not cross the
repository boundary.


**Related reports**

No exact earlier report of this cache-identity collision was found. Related but distinct issues include #1126 (shared-clone sparse-checkout race with the same user-facing missing-subdirectory symptom), #1498 (nested GitLab paths through Artifactory), and #1519 (deep GitLab subgroup paths in marketplace sources).

title: [BUG] `apm outdated` / `apm update` report `unknown` for Azure DevOps deps — `LockedDependency.to_dependency_ref()` drops `ado_*` fields (distinct from #2150 / #2119)
body:
### Summary

On **v0.25.0** (which already includes the ADO auth fixes from #2150 and #2119), `apm outdated` still reports `unknown` for every Azure DevOps dependency, and `apm update` cannot resolve semver ranges against ADO. This is **not** the auth-scheme issue from #2150 nor the URL-suffix issue from #2119 — both of those are fixed in this build.

Root cause: `LockedDependency.to_dependency_ref()` rebuilds a `DependencyReference` from the lockfile **without** the ADO coordinate fields (`ado_organization`, `ado_project`, `ado_repo`). The rebuilt ref reports `is_azure_devops() == True` (host-only check) but those fields are `None`, so `to_github_url()` calls `urllib.parse.quote(None)` → `TypeError`. The exception is swallowed by the `except Exception:` handlers in the outdated/update paths, degrading the result to `unknown`.

### Key distinguishing evidence (rules out #2150 / #2119)

On the **same** v0.25.0 install with an active `az login` session (no `ADO_APM_PAT` set):

- ✅ `apm view "dev.azure.com/{org}/{project}/{repo}" versions` — **works**, lists `v1.0.0`, `v1.1.0`, etc. (builds the ref via `DependencyReference.parse()`, which populates `ado_*`).
- ✅ `git ls-remote` against the same repo — works.
- ❌ `apm outdated` — `unknown`, with an **empty Source column**.
- ❌ `apm update` (with `ref: ^1.0.0`) — resolves to `-` and prints "No dependency changes were applied".

If this were an auth problem (#2150 / #2119), `apm view versions` and `git ls-remote` would fail too. They don't — so the difference is purely how the dependency reference is reconstructed: `view` uses `parse()` (populates `ado_*`), while `outdated`/`update` use `to_dependency_ref()` (leaves `ado_*` as `None`).

### Environment

- APM version: `0.25.0` (build includes #2121 and #2155)
- Host: Azure DevOps (`dev.azure.com`); auth via `az login` bearer; `ADO_APM_PAT` unset
- OS: Windows

### Steps to reproduce

1. Add an Azure DevOps dependency pinned to a semver tag, e.g. `dev.azure.com/{org}/{project}/{repo}#v1.0.0`, where the repo has annotated tags `v1.0.0` and `v1.1.0`.
2. `apm install` (writes a lockfile entry with `host: dev.azure.com`, `repo_url: {org}/{project}/{repo}`, `resolved_ref: v1.0.0`).
3. Run `apm outdated`.

### Actual output

```
┃ Package               ┃ Current ┃ Latest ┃ Status  ┃ Source ┃
│ dev.azure.com/{org}/… │ v1.0.0  │ -      │ unknown │        │
[i] Some dependencies could not be checked (branch/commit refs)
```

The **empty Source column** is diagnostic: the check exited via the early `except` path (which builds an `OutdatedRow` without `source=`), not the tag-comparison path (which sets `source="git tags"`).

`apm update` with a `ref: ^1.0.0` range shows:

```
[~] {org}/{project}/{repo}
    ref: v1.0.0 -> ^1.0.0 (f2dee13 -> -)
  No dependency changes were applied.
```

The `-` (resolved commit) confirms the range resolved to nothing.

### Expected behavior

`apm outdated` should report `Latest = v1.1.0`, `Status = outdated`, `Source = git tags`, and `apm update` should resolve `^1.0.0` to `v1.1.0` — exactly as `apm view versions` already does for the same repo.

### Root cause analysis

**1. `LockedDependency.to_dependency_ref()`** — `src/apm_cli/deps/lockfile.py` (~L588–620) — copies `repo_url` / `host` but never sets the ADO fields, so they default to `None`:

```python
def to_dependency_ref(self) -> DependencyReference:
    ...
    return DependencyReference(
        repo_url=self.repo_url,
        host=self.host,
        host_type=self.host_type,
        port=self.port,
        reference=ref,
        virtual_path=self.virtual_path,
        is_virtual=self.is_virtual,
        artifactory_prefix=self.registry_prefix,
        ...
        # ado_organization / ado_project / ado_repo NOT set → None
    )
```

**2. `is_azure_devops()`** — `src/apm_cli/models/dependency/reference.py` — is host-only:

```python
def is_azure_devops(self) -> bool:
    return self.host is not None and is_azure_devops_hostname(self.host)
```

**3. `to_github_url()`** — `src/apm_cli/models/dependency/reference.py` (~L2039) — builds the ADO URL exclusively from the (now `None`) fields:

```python
if self.is_azure_devops():
    project = urllib.parse.quote(self.ado_project, safe="")  # None → TypeError
    repo    = urllib.parse.quote(self.ado_repo, safe="")
    return f"https://{netloc}/{self.ado_organization}/{project}/_git/{repo}"
```

`urllib.parse.quote(None)` raises `TypeError`.

**4. Swallowed** — `src/apm_cli/commands/outdated.py::_check_one_dep`:

```python
try:
    remote_refs = downloader.list_remote_refs(dep_ref)
except Exception:
    return OutdatedRow(package=package_name, current=..., latest="-", status="unknown")  # no source=
```

The same failure occurs in the semver `resolve()` path used by `apm update` (`src/apm_cli/deps/git_reference_resolver.py`), where `list_remote_refs()` throws and the range resolves to nothing.

### Why existing tests miss it

`tests/unit/test_outdated_command.py::test_ado_dep_builds_correct_reference` fully mocks the downloader (`mock_downloader.list_remote_refs.return_value = [...]`), so it never constructs a real ADO URL and never hits `quote(None)`. It only asserts `list_remote_refs.assert_called_once()`. The test's docstring says ADO deps "should pass full URL to `DependencyReference.parse()`," but the actual code path calls `to_dependency_ref()`, not `parse()` — so the real URL construction is untested.

### Suggested fix

- Repopulate the ADO coordinates in `LockedDependency.to_dependency_ref()` — derive `ado_organization` / `ado_project` / `ado_repo` by splitting `repo_url` (`org/project/repo`) when the host is Azure DevOps.
- Additionally harden `to_github_url()` to fall back to splitting `repo_url` when the ADO fields are `None`, so a partially-populated ADO ref can never crash the URL builder.
- Add a regression test that exercises the **real** (non-mocked) ADO URL construction from a lockfile-rebuilt ref.

### Related (already fixed, different root cause)

- #2150 — semver install/update dropped the ADO bearer auth scheme (`install/helpers/ref_reuse.py`).
- #2119 — ADO marketplace `sourceBase` `.git` suffix + az-bearer fallback.

Both were fixed in v0.25.0; this report is a separate defect in the lockfile-rebuild path.

title: Formalize a spec requirement for uninstall reachability preservation (req-lk-0XX)
body:
## Context

PR #2269 fixes a confirmed defect: `apm uninstall` deleted a shared transitive dependency (`_local/shared`) still declared/reachable by a surviving direct dependency, because `LockedDependency.resolved_by` is single-valued (first-wins) and `commands/uninstall/engine.py::_build_children_index()` used it as an implicit (and here wrong) reachability oracle.

The fix adds `src/apm_cli/deps/reachability.py` (~245 lines): an additive, read-only forward-reachability walker from surviving direct dependencies, used by uninstall to decide what a candidate orphan may safely keep. No lockfile schema change; `resolved_by`/`local_path` stay `str | None` (repaired in place when a rescue changes which parent legitimately anchors a still-reachable entry, never widened to multi-parent storage).

## Why this issue exists

The repo's Mode B "silent-extension" spec-conformance gate (`tests/spec_conformance/mode_b_detector.sh`) flags `src/apm_cli/deps/` as a normative OpenAPM v0.1 critical path ("resolver"). PR #2269 lands substantive new behavior there without a corresponding spec anchor, so it was shipped with an explicit `apm-spec-waiver:` per `CONTRIBUTING.md`'s "Mode B (silent extension)" guidance -- this is a genuine bug fix restoring intended/expected uninstall behavior, not a new user-facing capability, and CONTRIBUTING.md documents the waiver mechanism for exactly this class of change ("true refactor / perf rewrite / internal cleanup with no observable behaviour delta" is the literal text, though this fix does have an observable behavior delta in the sense that it corrects a bug -- see PR discussion for the full judgment call).

The existing `req-lk-020` (added in spec v0.1.13, per the spec's own changelog table) already covers an adjacent but narrower case: *"the consumer MUST preserve any path freshly deployed by an active dependency in the current install, even when the same path is also recorded by a prior lockfile entry under a different dependency identity"* (deployed-file reconciliation during install). It does **not** explicitly cover the case this PR fixes: a transitive **lockfile dependency entry** (not just a deployed file path) that remains reachable from a surviving declared parent must not be removed during `uninstall`'s orphan-cleanup pass, even when its recorded `resolved_by` names a package that was just removed.

## Ask

Author a proper OpenAPM v0.1 requirement (likely `req-lk-021` or the next free `req-lk-0XX`) documenting:

1. During uninstall-time orphan cleanup, a conforming consumer implementation MUST NOT remove a transitive dependency lockfile entry that remains reachable (via forward reachability from the manifest's surviving declared dependencies) even though its recorded `resolved_by` names a package being removed in the same operation.
2. When such an entry is rescued, its `resolved_by` (and, for local deps, `local_path`) MUST be repaired to name a still-valid surviving parent, since a stale anchor would otherwise silently corrupt the entry's resolvability on a later uninstall.
3. If reachability cannot be established for a candidate (unreadable/malformed/missing manifest, or a resolved install path that fails containment validation), the consumer MUST fail closed -- preserve the candidate rather than delete it -- and surface this to the user.

This should land as its own spec-editorial PR (with the matching `docs/public/specs/manifests/openapm-v0.1.requirements.yml` + Appendix C row and a `@pytest.mark.req("req-lk-0XX")` conformance test under `tests/spec_conformance/`), mirroring how `req-lk-020` itself was introduced as a defensive-clarification spec release (v0.1.13) rather than gating the original code fix. This mirrors `apm-spec-guardian`'s intended review path for spec changes.

## References

- PR: #2269
- Implementation: `src/apm_cli/deps/reachability.py`, `src/apm_cli/commands/uninstall/engine.py`
- Existing adjacent requirement: [req-lk-020](../blob/main/docs/src/content/docs/specs/openapm-v0.1.md#req-lk-020)
- Gate: `tests/spec_conformance/mode_b_detector.sh`, `CONTRIBUTING.md` "Mode B (silent extension)"

body:
## CLI Consistency Report — Installation Failure

**Date**: 2026-07-17
**APM Version**: N/A — installation failed
**Commands Inspected**: 0

### Summary

The automated CLI consistency checker workflow was unable to install APM CLI because the execution sandbox has all outbound network traffic blocked (HTTP 403 from proxy on every pip/curl request). No Python packages could be downloaded from PyPI.

### Installation Failure Evidence

```
$ pip install -e .
warning: spurious network error (3 tries remaining): [7] Could not connect to server
  (CONNECT tunnel failed, response 403)
...
× Encountered error while generating package metadata.
╰─> ast-serialize
ERROR: metadata-generation-failed
```

```
$ pip install --no-index -e .
ERROR: No matching distribution found for setuptools>=42
```

No cached wheels were available in the environment. The system Python (PyPy 3.11) had no third-party packages installed. All CPython installations under `/opt/hostedtoolcache/Python/` only had pip itself.

### Root Cause

The agentic workflow sandbox blocks outbound HTTPS connections (proxy returns 403), preventing pip from downloading the APM CLI dependencies:
- `click`, `rich`, `pyyaml`, `requests`, `ruamel.yaml`, `gitpython`, etc.

### Impact

The CLI consistency checker — which is supposed to run `apm --help`, `apm init --help`, etc. and cross-reference with documentation — could not run any checks.

### Suggested Fix

To make the CLI consistency checker workflow runnable in this sandbox, one of the following approaches is needed:

1. **Pre-install APM CLI in the workflow setup steps** (`.apm/copilot-setup-steps.yml`) before the agent runs — install all dependencies during the setup phase where network may be available.
2. **Use a pre-built APM binary** (e.g., from a release artifact) placed on `PATH` during workflow setup.
3. **Bundle a pip wheel cache** or use `uv` with a local cache directory populated during setup steps.

The consistency checker logic itself is correct and will work once the CLI is installed and on `PATH`.

### Medium Severity

#### `apm update` docs have an incomplete target list

- **Command**: `apm update`
- **Problem**: The `--target` option in `docs/src/content/docs/reference/cli/update.md` lists only 8 valid target values, but the CLI accepts 20. The 12 omitted targets are valid inputs that will silently work but are not discoverable from the documentation.
- **Evidence**:

  Doc (`update.md`, options table):
  ```
  Accepts a single value (`claude`, `copilot`, `cursor`, `windsurf`, `kiro`, `codex`, `opencode`, `gemini`)
  ```

  Actual `apm update --help`:
  ```
  -t, --target TARGET  Agent target(s) to update for. Values: agent-
                       skills, agents, agy, all, antigravity, claude,
                       codex, copilot, copilot-app, copilot-cowork,
                       cursor, gemini, hermes, intellij, kiro,
                       openclaw, opencode, vscode, windsurf.
  ```

  Targets missing from the doc: `agent-skills`, `agents`, `agy`, `all`, `antigravity`, `copilot-app`, `copilot-cowork`, `hermes`, `intellij`, `openclaw`, `vscode`

- **Suggested Fix**: Replace the inline target list in `update.md` with the full set from the CLI, matching the format used in `install.md` (which already lists all values).

---

### Low Severity

#### Flag naming inconsistency: `--parallel-downloads` vs `--parallel-checks`

- **Commands**: `apm install`, `apm update`, `apm lock` vs `apm outdated`
- **Problem**: Three commands use `--parallel-downloads INTEGER` to limit concurrency; `apm outdated` uses `--parallel-checks INTEGER` with a unique `-j` short flag. While they control different underlying operations, users who expect a single consistent pattern across the CLI will find this surprising.
- **Evidence**:

  `apm install --help`: `--parallel-downloads INTEGER  Max concurrent package downloads (0 to disable parallelism)  [default: 4]`

  `apm outdated --help`: `-j, --parallel-checks INTEGER  Max concurrent remote checks (default: 4, 0 = sequential)`

- **Suggested Fix**: Either rename `--parallel-checks` to `--parallel-downloads` for consistency (with a deprecation alias), or add a note in the `apm outdated` reference doc explaining the naming difference. The `-j` short flag also has no analogue elsewhere in the CLI.

#### `apm deps update` has a stale target list (deprecated command)

- **Command**: `apm deps update`
- **Problem**: The deprecated `apm deps update` lists a narrower set of `--target` values than its replacement `apm update`. Users migrating to `apm update` may not realize additional targets are supported, and users still on the deprecated path cannot reach newer targets.
- **Evidence**:

  copilot, claude, cursor, opencode, codex, gemini, antigravity, windsurf, kiro, agent-skills, all

  copilot-cowork, cursor, gemini, hermes, intellij, kiro, openclaw, opencode, vscode, windsurf
  ```

  Missing from `apm deps update`: `agents`, `agy`, `copilot-app`, `copilot-cowork`, `hermes`, `intellij`, `openclaw`, `vscode`

- **Suggested Fix**: Since `apm deps update` is already deprecated, update its `--target` help text to reflect the current full target list so it matches `apm update`, or add a note that some targets require using `apm update` directly.

#### `apm config` description ends with a period; other command descriptions do not

- **Command**: `apm config`
- **Problem**: Minor punctuation inconsistency in help text style.
- **Evidence**:

  `apm config --help`: `Configure APM CLI.` (trailing period)

  All other top-level command descriptions (sampled): `Manage APM package dependencies`, `Initialize a new APM project`, `Install APM and MCP dependencies...`, `Refresh APM dependencies to the latest matching refs` -- no trailing period.

- **Suggested Fix**: Remove the trailing period from the `apm config` description string to match the rest of the CLI.

---

### Clean Areas

The following commands and areas passed all checks:

- **Error handling**: All tested commands (`apm install --nonexistent-flag`, `apm deps info` with missing arg, `apm config set` with missing args, `apm mcp show` with missing arg) produce clean usage + error messages with no stack traces.

- **`apm mcp` subcommands**: `search`, `show`, `install`, `list` -- default values (list: 20, search: 10) match between CLI and docs.
- **`apm config` subcommands**: `get`, `set`, `list`, `unset` -- all present in CLI and documented accurately.
- **`apm runtime` subcommands**: `setup`, `list`, `status`, `remove` -- all present and consistent with `runtime.md`.

- **`--dry-run` flag**: Consistently named and described across `install`, `update`, `uninstall`, `compile`, `deps clean`.

title: [FEATURE] Extend the scripts via agent package or even extend the apm cli
body:
**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**
We would like to create agent packages with code that runs deterministic logic. For example scaffolding something. Currently I see no way to automatically provide this deterministic script via an agent package.

**Describe the solution you'd like**
One way would be that the `scripts` of a package can automatically be added to the `script` of a projects `apm.yml` via a flag in the projects `apm.yml` or a separate `publicScripts` or something similar.
Another way could be that the package could contain an additional `cli-commands.yml` or similar that contains a lightweight description of cli commands that are added via the script and how they are called. Here is a very crude draft how that could look like:
```yaml
entryPoint: mypackage # The base command to use, eg. here it can be called with apm cli mypackage or even just apm mypackage <further arguments>
defaultRunner: my-cli # A runnable binary my-cli in the package/cli folder
commands:
- list:
    description: Lists the entries
- scaffold:
    description: Creates a new entry based on the templates
    arguments:
      - name:
          description: The name of the scaffolded entry
- someOtherCommand:
    runner: node ./scripts/mycommand.js # this command uses another runner, namely node and which runs the defined script from the packages script folder
```
and then, apm will read that specification and can provide the commands directly via the `apm` command.

**Describe alternatives you've considered**
Manually adding the scripts to the main `apm.yml` or describing in the `SKILL.md` how the commands can be called.

title: Allow SkillSpector --baseline through apm audit external args
body:
### Problem

`apm audit` supports scanner-specific `--external-args`, but the SkillSpector adapter in APM 0.26.0 does not allowlist SkillSpector’s `--baseline` option. As a result, repositories cannot use SkillSpector’s reviewed baseline suppression while retaining `apm audit` as the single audit and SARIF entry point.

The desired invocation is:

```sh
apm audit --external skillspector --no-external-llm \
  --external-args "--baseline .skillspector-baseline.yaml" \
  --format sarif --output reports/skillspector.sarif
```

APM audit reference: https://microsoft.github.io/apm/reference/cli/audit/

SkillSpector suppression reference: https://github.com/NVIDIA/SkillSpector/blob/main/docs/SUPPRESSION.md

### Requested behavior

- Allow the long-form `--baseline` option for the SkillSpector adapter.
- Require exactly one path value.
- Resolve and validate that path using APM’s existing external-argument safety checks.
- Reject paths outside the audit working directory.
- Continue rejecting arbitrary SkillSpector arguments fail-closed.

### Suggested tests

- Accept an existing baseline path inside the working directory.
- Reject a missing value.
- Reject an absolute or relative path that escapes the working directory.
- Preserve the current behavior when no baseline is supplied.
- Confirm SARIF output excludes findings suppressed by the supplied baseline.

This would let consumers adopt exact-fingerprint SkillSpector baselines without bypassing APM or patching installed packages.

title: [FEATURE] named dependency profiles in apm.yml
body:
# Feature request: named dependency profiles in `apm.yml`

## Problem

`apm.yml` only supports two dependency buckets: `dependencies` (always
installed) and `devDependencies` (excluded from `apm pack`). There's no
way to scope packages to a specific workflow stage (e.g. debugging,
load-testing, security-audit) without permanently keeping them in the
manifest or managing them by hand.

## Proposal

Add optional named profiles alongside the default dependency groups:

```yaml
dependencies: apm:
    - microsoft/apm-sample-package#v1.0.0

profiles: 
  debug:
    apm:
      - my-org/debug-toolkit
    mcp:
      - my-org/debugger-mcp
```

### Switching profiles locally would:

1. Install  dependencies  (+  devDependencies  if applicable) as usual.
2. Install the packages under the selected profile (e.g.  debug ).
3. Remove/uninstall packages belonging to any other profile that are
currently deployed locally.

### Suggested CLI surface:

```
apm install --profile debug   # install default + debug, prune other profiles
apm install                   # back to default only, profile packages removed
```

Profile switches should only affect the local install ( apm_modules/ ,
lockfile, deployed files) — not the manifest itself, and not what ships
via  apm pack .

### Motivation

Lets a package define optional, mutually-exclusive-ish tooling per
SDLC phase (debug, perf, security, etc.) in one  apm.yml , instead of
maintaining separate manifests or manually adding/removing dependencies
when switching contexts.

title: [BUG] `apm install` ignores global target configuration for MCP/LSP integrations and silently fails (Exits 0)
body:
**Describe the bug**
When a user configures a global default target using `apm config target` (e.g., `apm config target claude`), running `apm install` without the `--target` CLI option correctly installs APM packages but **silently skips writing MCP/LSP configurations**. 

The command exits cleanly with status code `0`, and no meaningful error message is displayed regarding the skipped MCP writes. The same issue applies to `apm update`.

**To Reproduce**
Steps to reproduce the behavior:
Run the following commands in any terminal:
```bash
mkdir tmp && cd tmp
echo -e "name: repro\nversion: 1.0.0" > apm.yml
apm config set target claude
apm install --mcp my-server -- node server.js
```

See error: The MCP configuration is skipped with a `No harness detected` (or `AmbiguousHarnessError`) warning, and says `Install interrupted`, but the command still exits with code `0`.

**Expected behavior**
`apm install` (and `apm update`) should respect the global default target set by `apm config target` when configuring MCP and LSP servers, just as it does during the APM package deployment phase. Additionally, if MCP/LSP config writes are skipped due to an unresolvable target ambiguity, the command should fail with a non-zero exit code if MCP/LSP dependencies were expected to be installed.

**Environment (please complete the following information):**
 - OS: Windows (also impacts macOS/Linux)
 - Python Version: 3.11.9
 - APM Version: 0.26.0
 - VSCode Version (if relevant): N/A

**Logs**
```
$ apm config set target claude
[*] Default install target set to: claude

$ apm install --mcp my-server -- node server.js
+- MCP Servers (1)
[x] Skipping all MCP config writes -- could not resolve active targets.
[x] No harness detected

APM scanned for harness markers (.claude/, CLAUDE.md, .cursor/, .cursorrules, 
.github/copilot-instructions.md, .github/instructions/, .github/agents/, 
.github/prompts/, .github/hooks/, .codex/, .gemini/, GEMINI.md, .opencode/, 
.windsurf/, .kiro/) but found none in this project.

Previously APM defaulted to copilot; this is now explicit.

Fix with one of:

  apm targets                            # see all supported harnesses
  apm install <pkg> --target claude      # deploy to a specific harness
  apm install <pkg> --target copilot     # or any supported target

Or declare in apm.yml:

  targets:
    - claude
[+] Added MCP server 'my-server'
  transport: stdio
  apm.yml: /absolute/path/to/tmp/apm.yml
[!] Install interrupted after 0.1s.
```

**Additional context**
### Root Cause Analysis

1. **Parameter Mismatch in Command Handlers**: In `commands/install.py` and `commands/update.py`, the `InstallContext` passed to `_install_apm_packages` correctly resolves the global target via `get_install_target()` into `ctx.target_override`. However, the CLI option `ctx.target` (`None` when omitted) is passed directly to `run_mcp_integration` and `run_lsp_integration` (e.g., `explicit_target=ctx.target`).
2. **Missing Fallback in MCP Integrator**: `run_mcp_integration` passes `explicit_target=None` down to `MCPIntegrator._gate_project_scoped_runtimes`. Because `explicit_target` and `yaml_targets` are `None`, it calls `resolve_targets(root, flag=None, yaml_targets=None)`.
3. **Ambiguous Resolution & Silent Catch**: `resolve_targets` falls back to Priority 3 (auto-detecting signals from `project_root`). When `project_root` has multiple signals (or no signals), `resolve_targets` raises `AmbiguousHarnessError` or `NoHarnessError`. `_gate_project_scoped_runtimes` catches these exceptions, prints a warning, and returns an empty list `[]`. 
4. **Exit Code 0**: `MCPIntegrator.install` receives 0 targets, writes no configs, returns 0, and `apm install` exits cleanly with code `0`.

### Proposed Solution

Update `commands/install.py` and `commands/update.py` to pass the effective target (falling back to `get_install_target()`) to `run_mcp_integration` and `run_lsp_integration` when `ctx.target` is `None`:

```python
# In commands/install.py and commands/update.py
from apm_cli.config import get_install_target

effective_explicit_target = ctx.target or get_install_target()

mcp_count, mcp_apm_config = run_mcp_integration(
    ...
    explicit_target=effective_explicit_target,
    ...
)
```

**Related Issues**: 
- Related to the gate logic introduced in **#1335** (which implemented the plural `targets:` field and the skip-with-info behavior for non-active MCP runtimes). The global target config fallback is currently being dropped before reaching that gate.

title: [BUG] `applyTo` multi-glob handling is inconsistent in compile placement analysis
body:
**Describe the bug**
`applyTo` multi-glob handling is inconsistent across parsing and `apm compile` placement analysis. A comma-separated `applyTo` value such as `.opencode/**/*.md, .github/**/*.md, **/.apm/**/*.md` is being treated as a single pattern during placement analysis, resulting in zero matches and fallback placement into `.opencode`.

This appears inconsistent with the repository's current parser/tests, which indicate that comma-separated glob lists are intended to be supported for `applyTo`.

There is also a related inconsistency with YAML list syntax for `applyTo`: the parser currently normalizes list-valued `applyTo` by keeping only the first non-null element, so multi-pattern list form is not reliably preserved across the compilation pipeline.

**To Reproduce**
Steps to reproduce the behavior:
1. Create an instruction file with frontmatter like:
   ```md
   ---
   applyTo: ".opencode/**/*.md, .github/**/*.md, **/.apm/**/*.md"
   description: "authoring conventions"
   ---
   ```
2. Run `apm compile --dry-run` or placement analysis on a repository containing matching files under `.opencode/`, `.github/`, and `.apm/`.
3. Observe that the placement analysis displays the full comma-joined string as one pattern.
4. Observe zero matches and fallback behavior similar to: `matched no files - placing in '.opencode'`.

**Expected behavior**
A comma-separated `applyTo` value should be split into multiple glob patterns and matched using OR semantics, consistent with `parse_apply_to()` and its unit tests. Placement analysis and compile behavior should reflect those split patterns instead of treating the full comma-joined value as a single glob.

If YAML list syntax is considered supported, all list entries should also be preserved and handled consistently throughout the pipeline.

**Environment (please complete the following information):**
 - OS: 
 - Python Version: 
 - APM Version: 
 - VSCode Version (if relevant): 

**Logs**
Relevant repository evidence:

- `src/apm_cli/utils/patterns.py` documents `applyTo` as a glob or comma-separated list of globs and implements `parse_apply_to()` accordingly.
- `tests/unit/utils/test_patterns.py` includes tests for comma-separated multi-glob parsing.
- `src/apm_cli/compilation/context_optimizer.py` documents `pattern` as a glob or comma-separated list of globs in `_file_matches_pattern()`.
- `src/apm_cli/primitives/parser.py` still normalizes list-valued `applyTo` by returning only the first list entry, which seems inconsistent with multi-pattern support.

Observed output/behavior reported during placement analysis:
- the effective rule shows `applyTo` as a single comma-joined string
- placement analysis reports 0 matches
- fallback warning: `matched no files - placing in '.opencode'`

**Additional context**
This looks like an inconsistency between the documented/tested `applyTo` semantics and at least one compile/placement path. If comma-separated multi-glob is intended behavior, the placement analysis path should be aligned. If not, the current parser/tests/docs should be updated to avoid signaling support that does not work end-to-end.

title: [FEATURE] skills and agents versioning
body:
**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**

title: [cli-consistency] CLI Consistency Report -- 2026-07-27
body:
## CLI Consistency Report

**Date**: 2026-07-27
**APM Version**: 0.26.0 (634f7b6)
**Commands Inspected**: 28 (top-level + all core/subcommands including mcp list, runtime remove/list/status, deps why, config unset)

### Summary

| Severity | Count |
|----------|-------|
| High | 0 |
| Medium | 3 |
| Low | 3 |

---

### Medium Severity

#### 1. `apm deps update --target` has a stale, incomplete target list

- **Command**: `apm deps update`
- **Problem**: The `--target` flag in `apm deps update` lists an outdated subset of targets. It is missing several targets available in `apm update`, `apm install`, and `apm compile`.
- **Evidence**:

`apm deps update --help` shows:
```
-t, --target TARGET  Target platform (comma-separated). Values:
                     copilot, claude, cursor, opencode, codex,
                     gemini, antigravity, windsurf, kiro, agent-
                     skills, all. 'agent-skills' deploys to ...
```

`apm update --help` (the non-deprecated replacement) shows:
```
-t, --target TARGET  Agent target(s) to update for. Values: agent-
                     skills, agents, agy, all, antigravity, claude,
                     codex, copilot, copilot-app, copilot-cowork,
                     cursor, gemini, hermes, intellij, kiro,
                     openclaw, opencode, vscode, windsurf.
```

Missing from `deps update`: `agents`, `agy`, `vscode`, `intellij`, `openclaw`, `hermes`, `copilot-app`, `copilot-cowork`.

- **Suggested Fix**: Update the target list in `apm deps update` to match the full list (same as `apm update`), or add a note in the deprecation message pointing users directly to `apm update` for the full target list. Since the command is deprecated, the simplest fix is adding a prominent note that the target list is incomplete and users should switch to `apm update`.

---

#### 2. `apm mcp install --help` forwards only a partial list of install options with unclear scope

- **Command**: `apm mcp install`
- **Problem**: The help text lists forwarded options inline but omits significant install flags (`--target`, `-g/--global`, `--ssh`, `--https`, `--allow-insecure`, `--skill`, etc.). The note "(see 'apm install --help' for the full list)" is confusing -- it implies those listed are a representative subset of everything that is forwarded, but users cannot tell which flags `apm mcp install` actually supports without testing.
- **Evidence**:

```
  Forwarded install options (see 'apm install --help' for the full list):
    --transport [stdio|http|sse|streamable-http]
    --url URL           Server URL for remote transports
    --env KEY=VALUE     Environment variable (repeatable)
    --header KEY=VALUE  HTTP header (repeatable)
    --registry URL      Custom registry URL
    --mcp-version VER   Pin registry entry to a specific version
    --dev / --dry-run / --force / --verbose / --no-policy
```

`--target` is not listed but is a common option users would want. It is unclear if `apm mcp install --target claude` would work.

- **Suggested Fix**: Either (a) list ALL forwarded options explicitly in `apm mcp install --help` (removing the vague "see full list" note), or (b) add `--target TARGET` and other commonly needed flags to the forwarded options list, and clarify which options are NOT forwarded.

---

#### 3. `--verbose` flag is missing from several `apm deps` subcommands, inconsistently present within the same group

- **Command**: `apm deps list`, `apm deps tree`, `apm deps info`, `apm deps clean`
- **Problem**: The `apm deps update` subcommand has `-v, --verbose`, but `list`, `tree`, `info`, and `clean` do not. This is inconsistent within the same command group. Users who expect verbose mode on `apm deps list` (which produces tabular output) will find none available.
- **Evidence**:

`apm deps update --help`:
```
  -v, --verbose  Show detailed update information
```

`apm deps list --help`:
```
Options:
  -g, --global  List user-scope dependencies (~/.apm/) instead of project
  --all         Show both project and user-scope dependencies
  --insecure    Show only installed dependencies locked to (redacted) sources
  --help        Show this message and exit.
```
(No `--verbose` option.)

Same for `apm deps tree --help`, `apm deps info --help`, and `apm deps clean --help`.

- **Suggested Fix**: Add `-v, --verbose` to `apm deps list`, `apm deps tree`, and `apm deps info` to show more detailed output (e.g., source URLs, resolved refs, primitive file paths). For `apm deps clean`, verbose is less critical but could show which directories/files were deleted.

---

### Low Severity

#### 4. `--verbose` descriptions are inconsistent in style across commands

- **Problem**: The `--verbose` flag has meaningfully different descriptions on every command, varying between generic and specific with no pattern.
- **Evidence**:
  - `apm init`: `Show detailed output`
  - `apm install`: `Show detailed installation information`
  - `apm uninstall`: `Show detailed removal information`
  - `apm update`: `Show unchanged deps and detailed pipeline diagnostics`
  - `apm compile`: `Show detailed source attribution and optimizer analysis`
  - `apm deps update`: `Show detailed update information`
  - `apm run`: `Show detailed output`
  - `apm mcp search/show`: `Show detailed output`
- **Suggested Fix**: Either standardize to a consistent short form (`Show detailed output`) for all commands, or keep the command-specific descriptions but ensure they all follow the same grammatical pattern (`Show detailed <X> output`).

---

#### 5. `--limit` default differs between `apm mcp list` (20) and `apm mcp search` (10)

- **Command**: `apm mcp list`, `apm mcp search`
- **Problem**: Two sibling subcommands under `apm mcp` use the same `--limit` flag with different defaults without explanation. This may surprise users who expect consistent pagination behavior across list/search in the same command group.
- **Evidence**:

`apm mcp list --help`:
```
  --limit INTEGER  Number of results to show  [default: 20]
```

`apm mcp search --help`:
```
  --limit INTEGER  Number of results to show  [default: 10]
```

- **Suggested Fix**: Align the defaults (both 10 or both 20), or add a parenthetical explaining why search shows fewer results by default (e.g., "search results are ranked so fewer is usually sufficient").

---

#### 6. `apm compile --all` description may mislead users into expecting truly all targets

- **Command**: `apm compile`
- **Problem**: `--all` is described as "Compile for all canonical targets. Equivalent to `--target all`." However, `--target all` explicitly excludes `antigravity`, `agent-skills`, and experimental targets. The word "all" in the flag name and description without a caveat could mislead users who expect it to cover every supported target.
- **Evidence**:

`apm compile --help`:
```
  --all    Compile for all canonical targets.
           Equivalent to --target all.
```

Same command, `--target` description:
```
  'antigravity' (alias 'agy')
  deploys to .agents/ and is explicit-only --
  not part of 'all'. 'all' excludes
  antigravity and experimental targets;
  combine explicit-only targets when needed.
```

- **Suggested Fix**: Add a parenthetical to the `--all` description: "Compile for all canonical targets (excludes antigravity, agent-skills, and experimental targets). Equivalent to `--target all`."

---

### Clean Areas

The following commands and areas passed all checks with no issues found:

- **Error handling**: All tested commands (`apm install --nonexistent-flag`, `apm deps info` with no arg, `apm config set` with no args) produced clean, non-crash error messages with a usage hint. No tracebacks observed.
- **`apm init`, `apm uninstall`, `apm update`, `apm compile`, `apm run`**: Help text is clear, well-structured, and technically accurate.
- **`apm mcp search`, `apm mcp show`**: Help text is accurate and consistent with docs.
- **`apm config set/get/list/unset`**: All four subcommands present and documented. Behavior matches docs.
- **`apm runtime setup/list/status/remove`**: All four subcommands present. `remove` correctly exposes `-y/--yes` as documented.
- **`apm deps why`, `apm deps clean`**: Present in both CLI and docs with matching descriptions.
- **Documentation coverage**: All commands visible in `apm --help` have corresponding pages under `docs/src/content/docs/reference/cli/`. No undocumented commands found, no docs-only ghost commands.
- **`--help` / `-h` flag**: Works correctly on every tested command and subcommand.
- **`--dry-run` naming**: Consistent (`--dry-run`, not `--dryrun`) across all commands that support it (`install`, `uninstall`, `update`, `compile`, `deps clean`, `deps update`).
- **`-g/--global` naming**: Consistent across all commands that support it.

title: [perf-scan] 2026-07-28 -- performance opportunities found
body:
## Performance Scan - 2026-07-28

Automated scan of src/apm_cli/ for algorithmic performance anti-patterns.
2 finding(s) identified.

### Findings

#### [A] Quadratic Lockfile Scan -- src/apm_cli/commands/uninstall/engine.py:237-269

- Current: O(n*m) -- for each package in `packages`, two sequential linear scans over `lockfile.dependencies.values()` (up to m entries each), looking for matching `discovered_via` and `marketplace_plugin_name` attributes.
- Proposed: O(n+m) -- pre-build two lookup dicts keyed by `(discovered_via, marketplace_plugin_name)` and `marketplace_plugin_name` once before the outer loop, then do O(1) dict lookups per package.
- Fix: Before the `for package in packages:` loop at line 237, build `by_both = {(d.discovered_via, d.marketplace_plugin_name): d for d in lockfile.dependencies.values()}` and `by_name = {d.marketplace_plugin_name: d for d in lockfile.dependencies.values()}`, then replace the inner `for dep in lockfile.dependencies.values():` scans with direct dict lookups.

#### [C] json.dumps Dedup Key in Per-Entry Loop -- src/apm_cli/integration/hook_integrator.py:1595-1604

- Current: O(k * S) -- `json.dumps({"s": source, "c": cmp}, sort_keys=True)` is called once per hook entry (k entries) where S is the serialization cost proportional to entry size; called during every multi-source hook merge, which runs per-package-per-target.
- Proposed: O(k) with cheaper hashing -- replace json serialization with a hashable tuple key: `(source, tuple(sorted(cmp.items())))`, which avoids the encoder overhead and allocates no intermediate JSON string.
- Fix: Replace `dedup_key = _json.dumps({"s": source, "c": cmp}, sort_keys=True)` at line 1601 with `dedup_key = (source, tuple(sorted(cmp.items())))` and update `seen_keys` to `set()` of tuples (the existing set membership test works unchanged).

### Scan coverage

- src/apm_cli/ (418 files scanned)
- Patterns checked: A (quadratic loops), B (linear scan in loop),
  C (unconditional expensive ops), D (redundant config parsing),
  E (heavy top-level imports), F (sequential independent I/O)

title: [BUG] --target vscode drops v0.1 `value`-shaped runtime arguments for npm/pypi/generic launchers
body:
**Describe the bug**

`apm install --target vscode` silently drops MCP Registry v0.1 `runtimeArguments` for npm, pypi, and generic-runtime packages. The launcher written to `.vscode/mcp.json` still starts, but every flag the registry declared is missing, and the same server configured for Copilot keeps them.

This is the non-container remainder of #2377. The container path was fixed in #2387 with a dedicated builder; the npm/pypi/generic branches were deliberately left out of that PR because fixing them requires a semantic decision (below), not just reading another key.

**To Reproduce**

Registry package (v0.1 shape, `value` beside a `type` — as normalized by `_normalize_v0_1_package`):

```json
{
  "name": "@scope/mcp-server",
  "registry_name": "npm",
  "runtime_hint": "npx",
  "runtime_arguments": [
    {"value": "--stdio", "type": "positional"},
    {"value": "--config", "type": "positional"},
    {"value": "./mcp.yaml", "type": "positional"}
  ]
}
```

Rendered configs for the same package:

```
vscode : npx ['-y', '@scope/mcp-server']                                      <- flags gone
copilot: npx ['-y', '@scope/mcp-server', '--stdio', '--config', './mcp.yaml']
```

Same for pypi: vscode renders `uvx ['mcp-server-fetch']` while copilot renders `uvx ['mcp-server-fetch', '--ignore-robots-txt']`.

Proof that this is a spelling gap rather than a vscode design choice: the identical arguments authored in the legacy `value_hint` spelling ARE honoured by the vscode npm branch:

```
vscode (value_hint spelling): npx ['-y', '@scope/mcp-server', '--stdio', '--config', './mcp.yaml']
```

**Root cause**

`VSCodeClientAdapter._extract_package_args` walks `runtime_arguments` reading only `value_hint` (`src/apm_cli/adapters/client/vscode.py`); v0.1 entries carry `value`, so extraction returns `[]` and each branch synthesizes its minimal launcher from the package name.

**Why the fix needs a design decision first**

The extractor's empty return is a load-bearing signal, and the branches disagree about what a non-empty extraction means:

- vscode npm: `["-y", name] + extracted` — name is always synthesized, so extending the extractor is safe here.
- vscode pypi/generic: `args = extracted` **verbatim** — the extraction is treated as the complete argv. A v0.1 package whose runtime args don't include the package name (the common case; the name is the package identifier) would render `uvx --python 3.12` with no package at all.
- copilot pypi (`_apply_pypi_homebrew_generic_config`): always `[package_name] + runtime + package` — name is prepended unconditionally.

So either the vscode pypi/generic branches align with copilot's name-prepend semantics (which changes behavior for legacy `value_hint` data that embeds its own name — those would need dedup), or they keep verbatim semantics and merge the name conditionally. That choice affects existing registry data and should be settled before the code is touched.

**Expected behavior**

A v0.1 registry package renders the same argv on `--target vscode` as it does on Copilot-family targets, with the package name appearing exactly once.

**Environment**
- APM version: main (post #2387)
- Applies to all OSes

This behavior is not mentioned in the CLI help at all, so users must consult the documentation to discover it.
- **Evidence**:
  ```
  # apm config get --help
  Usage: apm config get [OPTIONS] [KEY]
    Get a configuration value
  Options:
    --help  Show this message and exit.
  ```
  Docs say: *"With no argument, prints the user config summary: effective values for core user-settable keys."*
- **Suggested Fix**: Update the help text to: `"Get a configuration value. With no KEY, prints the full user config summary (same as 'apm config list')."` This matches the documentation and makes the optional-key behavior discoverable.

---

#### `--target` flag name inconsistently described as "platform" vs "harness" vs "target"

- **Command**: `apm deps update`, `apm compile`, `apm install`, `apm update`
- **Problem**: The terminology used to describe what `--target` selects changes between commands: "platform", "harness", and "target". This is a terminology inconsistency that could confuse users learning the tool.
- **Evidence**: See Medium finding above for the four different phrasings.
- **Suggested Fix**: Pick one noun (suggest `"target"` to match the flag name itself and the existing `targets-matrix` documentation) and use it consistently in all help strings.

---

### Clean Areas

- **Error handling**: All tested error scenarios (`--nonexistent-flag`, missing required arguments) produce clean error messages with no stack traces.
- **`--help` / `-h`**: Works correctly on every command and subcommand inspected.
- **`-v, --verbose`**: Present and consistently named across all applicable commands (`init`, `install`, `uninstall`, `update`, `compile`, `run`, `deps update`, `mcp search`, `mcp show`, `mcp list`).
- **`--dry-run`**: Present and consistently named on `install`, `uninstall`, `update`, `compile`, `deps clean`.
- **`-y, --yes`**: Present on `update` and `deps clean` where applicable.
- **`-g, --global`**: Present and consistent across `install`, `uninstall`, `update`, `deps list`, `deps tree`, `deps update`, `compile`, `lock`.
- **`apm mcp` subcommands**: `mcp list`, `mcp search`, `mcp show`, `mcp install` all documented correctly and match the CLI interface. Default limits match (list: 20, search: 10).
- **`apm deps why`**: Present in CLI, documented in `deps.md`, consistent behavior description.

Users migrating from `apm deps update` to `apm update` may be surprised by the extra targets. The `deps update` help also describes `all` incorrectly -- it omits `copilot-app`, `copilot-cowork`, `hermes`, `intellij`, `openclaw`, `vscode`, and the `agents`/`agy` aliases that are live in `apm update`.
- **Evidence**:

  `apm deps update --help`:
  ```
  -t, --target TARGET  Target platform (comma-separated). Values:
                       copilot, claude, cursor, opencode, codex,
                       gemini, antigravity, windsurf, kiro, agent-
                       skills, all.
  ```

  `apm update --help`:
  ```
  -t, --target TARGET  Agent target(s) to update for. Values: agent-
                       skills, agents, agy, all, antigravity, claude,
                       codex, copilot, copilot-app, copilot-cowork,
                       cursor, gemini, hermes, intellij, kiro,
                       openclaw, opencode, vscode, windsurf.
  ```

  Missing from `deps update` target list: `agents`, `agy`, `copilot-app`, `copilot-cowork`, `hermes`, `intellij`, `openclaw`, `vscode`.
- **Suggested Fix**: Update the `--target` help string in `apm deps update` to match the canonical target list used across the rest of the CLI, or remove the inline list entirely and redirect the reader to `apm update --help` (since the command is already marked deprecated).

---

#### `apm install --target` deprecation note embeds a compile-specific caveat confusingly

- **Command**: `apm install`
- **Problem**: The `--target` flag help text inside `apm install --help` contains the sentence "For 'apm compile', use '--all'; '--target all' is deprecated." This sentence is about `apm compile`, not about `apm install`. A reader scanning `apm install --help` will read it as if `--target all` is deprecated for `install` as well, which is misleading. For `apm install`, `--target all` is still a valid, non-deprecated value.
- **Evidence**:

  ```

- **Suggested Fix**: Remove the "For 'apm compile', use '--all'; '--target all' is deprecated." sentence from `apm install`'s `--target` help text. If a cross-reference is desired, move it to the `apm compile --help` only, where it is already present.

---

title: [perf-scan] 2026-08-02 -- performance opportunities found
body:
## Performance Scan - 2026-08-02

Automated scan of src/apm_cli/ for algorithmic performance anti-patterns.
2 finding(s) identified.

### Findings

#### [B] Linear scan inside loop -- commands/uninstall/engine.py:472-504

- Current: O(packages * lockfile_size) -- for each package in the uninstall list, two sequential full scans of `lockfile.dependencies.values()` are performed (first-pass exact match at line 483, second-pass plugin_name fallback at line 493). With a 200-package lockfile and 10 packages to uninstall, this is ~4,000 dict-value iterations.
- Proposed: O(packages + lockfile_size) -- pre-build two lookup dicts from the lockfile once before the outer loop, then do O(1) lookups per package.
- Fix: Before the `for package in packages` loop, build `by_exact: dict[tuple[str,str], dep] = {(d.marketplace_plugin_name, d.discovered_via): d for d in lockfile.dependencies.values()}` and a fallback `by_plugin: dict[str, dep]`; replace both inner `for dep in lockfile.dependencies.values()` scans with dict lookups.

#### [D] Repeated env-var reads inside nested loop -- registry/operations.py:380-401

- Current: `os.getenv(var_name)` is called inside a triple-nested loop (outer: per `server_ref`, middle: per `package`, inner: per `env_var` dict entry). The same environment variable name can be read multiple times across server references, performing redundant syscalls on each iteration.
- Proposed: O(1) per lookup after a single snapshot -- snapshot `os.environ` once into a local dict before the `for server_ref in server_references` loop and replace `os.getenv(var_name)` with `env_snapshot.get(var_name)`.
- Fix: Add `env_snapshot = dict(os.environ)` before the loop at line 353 and replace `os.getenv(var_name)` at line 393 with `env_snapshot.get(var_name)`.

### Scan coverage

- src/apm_cli/ (425 files scanned)
- Patterns checked: A (quadratic loops), B (linear scan in loop),
  C (unconditional expensive ops), D (redundant config parsing),
  E (heavy top-level imports), F (sequential independent I/O)

title: [FEATURE] Add "copilot" marketplace output format for GitHub Copilot CLI
body:
**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**

When maintaining a plugin marketplace for GitHub Copilot CLI, the required `marketplace.json` schema differs from the Claude Code format that APM currently emits. Copilot CLI expects the marketplace version nested inside a `metadata` object (`metadata.version`, `metadata.description`) rather than at the top level, and plugin `source` as a relative path string rather than a `{type, repo, sha}` dict. There is no way today to produce a Copilot-CLI-compliant `marketplace.json` through `apm pack` — teams either hand-craft the file or maintain a separate post-processing step.

**Describe the solution you'd like**

Add a new `copilot` output profile alongside the existing `claude` and `codex` profiles. It should:

1. Default to `.github/plugin/marketplace.json` (the path Copilot CLI scans by default).
2. Emit the Copilot CLI marketplace format as documented at [docs.github.com/en/copilot/…/plugins-marketplace](https://docs.github.com/en/copilot/how-tos/copilot-cli/customize-copilot/plugins-marketplace):

```json
{
  "name": "my-marketplace",
  "owner": { "name": "Acme", "email": "plugins@acme.com" },
  "metadata": {
    "description": "Curated plugins for our team",
    "version": "1.0.0"
  },
  "plugins": [
    {
      "name": "frontend-design",
      "description": "...",
      "version": "2.1.0",
      "source": "./plugins/frontend-design"
    }
  ]
}
```

3. Be configurable in `apm.yml` like the other formats:

```yaml
marketplace:
  outputs:
    claude: {}
    copilot:
      path: .github/plugin/marketplace.json
```

4. Support path override at pack time via the existing `--marketplace-path` flag:

```sh
apm pack --marketplace-path copilot=.github/plugin/marketplace.json
```

Implementation would follow the same extension points used by `codex`:

- New `MarketplaceOutputProfile` (`name="copilot"`) in `output_profiles.py` with `path_env_var=APM_MARKETPLACE_COPILOT_PATH`.
- New `copilot` mapper in `output_mappers.py` that emits `metadata.{version,description}` and flat relative-path `source` strings on plugin entries (stripping APM-only fields like `sha`, `ref`, `tags`).
- New `MarketplaceCopilotConfig` dataclass in `yml_schema.py` and `copilot` added to `_APM_MARKETPLACE_KEYS`.

**Describe alternatives you've considered**

- **Post-processing script:** A separate script that reads the Claude output and reshapes it. Works but breaks the `--check-clean` gate and adds CI complexity.
- **Using `--marketplace-path claude=.github/plugin/marketplace.json`:** Gets the file to the right path but the format is still Claude's (top-level `version`, `source` as a dict), which Copilot CLI would silently misparse.
- **Hand-authoring the file:** Bypasses APM entirely and loses lockfile-driven resolution.

**Additional context**

- GitHub Copilot CLI marketplace schema reference: [docs.github.com/en/copilot/reference/copilot-cli-reference/cli-plugin-reference#marketplacejson](https://docs.github.com/en/copilot/reference/copilot-cli-reference/cli-plugin-reference#marketplacejson)
- Copilot CLI also looks for `marketplace.json` in `.claude-plugin/` as a fallback (noted in the docs), so teams running both Claude Code and Copilot CLI from one repo need a way to emit both formats from a single `apm.yml` — exactly what `outputs: {claude: {}, copilot: {}}` would enable.
- Key format differences between Claude and Copilot CLI outputs:

| Field | Claude format | Copilot CLI format |
|---|---|---|
| Marketplace version | top-level `version` | `metadata.version` |
| Marketplace description | top-level `description` | `metadata.description` |
| Plugin source | `{type, repo, sha, ...}` dict | relative path string |
| Plugin author/tags | supported | not in schema |

title: [BUG] `--check-versions` fails with `no_apm_yml` for Plugin collection (`plugin.json`) packages in a marketplace
body:
## Describe the bug

Running `apm pack --check-versions` on a marketplace where all packages use the **Plugin collection** layout (`plugin.json`, no `apm.yml`) fails with exit code `3`. Every package is reported as misaligned with reason `[no_apm_yml]`, even though the [APM docs](https://microsoft.github.io/apm/reference/package-types/#plugin-collection-pluginjson) explicitly say `apm.yml` is not required for this layout.

The version alignment gate only reads versions from `apm.yml`. It has no fallback to read the `version` field from `plugin.json`, so Plugin collection packages are unconditionally rejected as unresolvable.

## To Reproduce

1. Create a marketplace project with `apm.yml` using `versioning.strategy: tag_pattern`.
2. Add one or more local package entries whose `source` directories contain only `plugin.json` (Plugin collection layout) — no `apm.yml` in the package directory.
3. Run `apm pack --check-versions`.
4. Observe exit code `3` and `[no_apm_yml]` for every Plugin collection package.

Minimal reproducer structure:

```
my-marketplace/
├── apm.yml                        # marketplace root manifest
└── plugins/
    └── my-plugin/
        ├── plugin.json            # version: "1.2.3"
        └── skills/
            └── my-skill/
                └── SKILL.md
```

`apm.yml` (relevant excerpt):

```yaml
marketplace:
  versioning:
    strategy: tag_pattern
  build:
    tagPattern: "{name}-v{version}"
  packages:
    - name: my-plugin
      source: ./plugins/my-plugin
      version: 1.2.3
```

## Expected behavior

`apm pack --check-versions` should read the `version` field from `plugin.json` when `apm.yml` is absent in the package directory, consistent with the documented Plugin collection layout. All packages should pass alignment if `plugin.json["version"]` matches the marketplace entry version and satisfies the configured strategy.

## Environment

- OS: Windows
- Python Version: 3.9.16
- APM Version: 0.26.0

## Logs

```
[x] Version alignment failed [strategy=tag_pattern]
[i]     plugins/my-plugin  <none>  [no_apm_yml]
```

## Additional context

- The [Package Types reference](https://microsoft.github.io/apm/reference/package-types/#plugin-collection-pluginjson) states that Plugin collection packages do not require `apm.yml`.
- The [Layout summary](https://microsoft.github.io/apm/reference/package-types/#layout-summary) table lists `plugin.json` as the manifest for this layout, making it the authoritative version source.
- Affected strategies: at minimum `tag_pattern` (not tested with `lockstep` or `per_package`, but the same code path applies to both since `no_apm_yml` is caught before the strategy branch).

When I install MCP with passthrough fields, they're populated for claude, but missing for opencode.

I created sample package for opencode and claude that includes only one mcp with fields (`oauth` and `myField` that should be processed as passthrough fields according to the [documentation](https://microsoft.github.io/apm/consumer/install-mcp-servers/#the-mcp-section-in-apmyml).

name: test
version: 1.0.0
targets:
- opencode
- claude
dependencies:
  apm: []
  mcp: 
    - name: slack
      registry: false
      transport: http
      url: https://mcp.slack.com/mcp
      oauth:
        clientId: "<pre-registered-client-id>"
        callbackPort: 3118
      myField: somevalue
```

When I install it, these custom fields are included into configuration for claude, but missing in opencode config.

name: test

title: [BUG] apm update aborts the entire run when a SHA-pinned dependency has no annotated tag upstream
body:
**Describe the bug**

When a project has a dependency pinned to a commit SHA, and the upstream repository has no annotated tag containing that commit, `apm update` exits `1` during the revision-pin freshness check and never renders an update plan.

Every other dependency in the project is left untouched, including ones that are perfectly updatable. A single SHA-pinned dependency therefore freezes updates for the entire project.

Refusing to auto-promote a SHA pin to a branch or lightweight tag is reasonable. Making that refusal fatal for *unrelated* dependencies is what makes this a bug.

**To Reproduce**

1. Create a project whose `apm.yml` mixes a SHA-pinned dependency with a tag-pinned one. `github/awesome-copilot` publishes **no tags at all**, so a SHA pin against it can never be promoted:

```yaml
name: repro
version: 1.0.0
description: repro
author: repro
dependencies:
  apm:
    - github/awesome-copilot/skills/acquire-codebase-knowledge#6c7fe1b15f1be7e29d3aaf04fb3423ee5a226353
    - obra/superpowers#v6.2.0
  mcp: []
includes: auto
scripts: {}
```

2. Run `apm update --dry-run`
3. The run exits `1` with no plan rendered. `obra/superpowers` is updatable and is never even considered.

Control: delete the `awesome-copilot` line and re-run. The command then exits `0` and plans `obra/superpowers` normally, which isolates the SHA-pinned entry as the cause.

```console
$ apm update --dry-run ; echo "exit=$?"      # both deps
[>] Checking upstream for revision-pin freshness...
[x] No annotated tag found for revision-pinned dependency. ...
exit=1

$ apm update --dry-run ; echo "exit=$?"      # SHA-pinned dep removed
  [+] obra/superpowers
      ref: v6.2.0 (3dcbd5c, new)
  1 added
exit=0
```

**Expected behavior**

APM warns that the SHA-pinned dependency cannot be advanced, skips it, and continues to plan and update the remaining dependencies. A pin that cannot be promoted is a property of one dependency and should not gate the whole run.

**Environment (please complete the following information):**
 - OS: macOS 26.6 (arm64)
 - Python Version: 3.12 (standalone build) and 3.13 (PyPI `apm-cli` in a venv) — reproduces on both
 - APM Version: 0.28.0 (also reproduces on 0.27.0)
 - VSCode Version (if relevant): n/a

**Logs**

```
[>] Checking upstream for revision-pin freshness...
[x] No annotated tag found for revision-pinned dependency. APM will not replace
a SHA pin with a branch or lightweight tag.
```

Exit code `1`. No update plan is printed.

**Additional context**

*Workaround.* A targeted update bypasses the gate, so only bulk updates are blocked:

```bash
apm update <package-id>     # e.g. apm update superpowers
```

*Ref-form matrix.* Behaviour of each pin form, verified on 0.28.0:

| ref form | `apm pack` | `apm update` |
| --- | --- | --- |
| annotated tag | ok | ok |
| lightweight tag | ok | ok |
| raw commit SHA | ok | **fails, exit 1, aborts whole run** |
| branch (e.g. `main`) | rejected | ok |

*Misleading wording.* "No **annotated** tag found" reads as though annotated tags are required for a pin to be updatable. They are not — a lightweight tag works fine (`#v2.6.0` on a lightweight tag plans and updates cleanly). The annotated-tag requirement applies only to *promoting an existing SHA pin*. As written, the message sends users chasing annotated tags and GitHub Releases when a plain `git tag` would do.

*Related gap: branch refs are not an available workaround.* The natural response to this bug is to stop pinning SHAs and pin a branch instead. That is blocked from the other side — `apm pack` rejects branch refs and recommends a flag that does not exist:

```console
$ apm pack
Error: Package 'example' resolves to branch/HEAD ref 'main'. Branch refs are
mutable and not recommended for reproducible builds. Pin to a tag or SHA, or
pass --allow-head to override.

$ apm pack --allow-head
Error: No such option '--allow-head'.
```

`--allow-head` is also absent from `apm pack --help`. Happy to split this into its own issue if you'd prefer it tracked separately.

*Combined effect.* For a project or marketplace whose upstream publishes no tags, there is currently **no valid pin form**: a SHA breaks `apm update`, and a branch breaks `apm pack`. Tagging upstream is the only fix, which is not always in the consumer's control.

*Suggested fixes.*
1. Downgrade the revision-pin freshness failure to a per-dependency warning and continue the run.
2. Either implement `--allow-head` on `apm pack` or remove it from the error message.
3. Reword the message so it does not imply annotated tags are required as pins.

title: [BUG] --target copilot writes MCP configuration to unsupported .vscode/mcp.json
body:
### Description

Issue #2437 was closed because, at project scope, `--target copilot` intentionally resolves to VS Code and writes `.vscode/mcp.json`.

However, GitHub Copilot CLI has removed support for `.vscode/mcp.json`:

[Migration guidance](https://docs.github.com/en/copilot/reference/copilot-cli-reference/cli-command-reference#migrating-from-vscodemcpjson)

As a result, the documented APM behavior now produces MCP configuration that Copilot CLI does not discover or use.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Install an MCP server at project scope using `--target copilot`.
2. Observe that APM writes the configuration to `.vscode/mcp.json`.
3. Start GitHub Copilot CLI in the project.
4. Observe that the MCP server is not available.

### Expected behavior

`--target copilot` should write project-scoped configuration to a location supported by the current Copilot CLI, or APM should reject the target with a clear migration message.

The target-resolution contract should not route `copilot` to VS Code once Copilot CLI no longer supports `.vscode/mcp.json`.

### Actual behavior

`--target copilot` succeeds but writes configuration exclusively to `.vscode/mcp.json`, resulting in an unusable configuration for Copilot CLI.

### Related issue

This supersedes the behavior discussed in #2437. The original implementation may have matched the former target-resolution contract, but that contract is now incompatible with the Copilot CLI.

### References

- #2437
- [Copilot CLI: Migrating from `.vscode/mcp.json`](https://docs.github.com/en/copilot/reference/copilot-cli-reference/cli-command-reference#migrating-from-vscodemcpjson)

title: [cli-consistency] CLI Consistency Report -- 2026-08-06
body:
## CLI Consistency Report

**Date**: 2026-08-06
**APM Version**: 0.28.0 (3aa0365)
**Commands Inspected**: 51 (33 top-level + 6 `deps` + 4 `mcp` + 4 `config` + 4 `runtime`)

### Summary

| Severity | Count |
|----------|-------|
| High | 0 |
| Medium | 3 |
| Low | 2 |

---

### High Severity

None found. All CLI commands are present and match documentation. Error handling for invalid arguments produces clean error messages (no stack traces).

---

### Medium Severity

#### 1. Inconsistent deprecation style across commands

- **Commands**: `apm deps`, `apm init`
- **Problem**: `apm deps --help` displays `deps update` as `DEPRECATED:` (all-caps prefix), while `apm init --help` shows the deprecated `--plugin` and `--marketplace` flags as `(deprecated)` (lowercase, in parentheses). These are two different visual conventions for the same concept in the same CLI.
- **Evidence**:
  ```
  # apm deps --help (Commands section):
  update  DEPRECATED: use 'apm update' instead (strict superset).

  # apm init --help (Options section):
  --plugin         (deprecated) Use 'apm plugin init' instead. Scaffolds plugin.json + apm.yml.
  --marketplace    (deprecated) Use 'apm marketplace init' instead. Seeds a marketplace block.
  ```
- **Suggested Fix**: Adopt a single convention. The lowercase parenthetical `(deprecated)` style used in `apm init` is the more common Click/Typer pattern and reads more naturally in command listings. Update the `deps update` description to use the same style: `(deprecated) use 'apm update' instead (strict superset).`

---

#### 2. Inconsistent `--yes` / `-y` flag descriptions

- **Commands**: `apm update`, `apm deps clean`, `apm init`
- **Problem**: All three commands expose `-y, --yes` for the same purpose (skip a confirmation prompt), but describe it with different wording and varying detail levels.
- **Evidence**:
  ```
  # apm update
  -y, --yes    Skip the confirmation prompt (for CI / automation)

  # apm deps clean
  -y, --yes    Skip confirmation prompt

  # apm init
  -y, --yes    Skip interactive prompts and use auto-detected defaults
  ```
- **Suggested Fix**: Standardize to a single description. Suggested canonical form: `Skip the confirmation prompt`. Add `(for CI / automation)` only where non-interactive use is specifically important (e.g. `apm update`).

---

#### 3. Inconsistent `--verbose` / `-v` flag descriptions

- **Commands**: Multiple
- **Problem**: The `--verbose` flag carries different descriptions across commands, ranging from the generic two-word form to detailed multi-clause sentences.
- **Evidence**:
  ```
  # Generic (run, init, mcp search, mcp show):
  -v, --verbose    Show detailed output

  # Command-specific (install):
  -v, --verbose    Show detailed installation information

  # Command-specific (uninstall):
  -v, --verbose    Show detailed removal information

  # Long-form (update):
  -v, --verbose    Show unchanged deps and detailed pipeline diagnostics
  ```
- **Suggested Fix**: Use `Show detailed output` as the baseline. Where the command-specific meaning genuinely differs (e.g. `update`), keep the richer description. Standardize the remaining commands that use distinct but equivalent phrasings (`install`, `uninstall`) to `Show detailed output`.

---

### Low Severity

#### 4. `apm config set`, `config get`, and `config list` have no examples in help text

- **Commands**: `apm config set`, `apm config get`, `apm config list`
- **Problem**: These three subcommands display only a one-line description with no examples, accepted key names, or valid value hints. In contrast, `apm mcp install --help` shows examples inline, and the docs (`apm config` reference page) document a rich set of keys. A user running `apm config set --help` gets no guidance on what keys exist.
- **Evidence**:
  ```
  Usage: apm config set [OPTIONS] KEY VALUE

    Set a configuration value

  Options:
    --help  Show this message and exit.
  ```
- **Suggested Fix**: Add at least one example and a note pointing to valid keys. Example addition:
  ```
  Examples:
    apm config set target copilot
    apm config set self-update.channel prerelease
  Run 'apm config list' to see current values and available keys.
  ```

---

#### 5. `apm deps update` missing `--dry-run` flag

- **Command**: `apm deps update`
- **Problem**: `apm deps update` is a write operation (refreshes dependency refs) but lacks a `--dry-run` flag. All peer write commands (`apm update`, `apm install`, `apm compile`, `apm deps clean`) expose `--dry-run`. While `deps update` is deprecated, users still running it cannot preview changes safely without it.
- **Evidence**:
  ```
  # apm deps update --help Options section -- no --dry-run present
  Options:
    -v, --verbose                 Show detailed update information
    --force                       Overwrite locally-authored files on collision
    -t, --target TARGET           Target platform (comma-separated). ...
    --parallel-downloads INTEGER  ...
    -g, --global                  Update user-scope dependencies (~/.apm/)
    --legacy-skill-paths          ...
    --help                        Show this message and exit.

  # All other write commands have:
  --dry-run    (various descriptions)
  ```
- **Suggested Fix**: Add `--dry-run` to `deps update` so deprecated users can preview before migrating. Alternatively, add a note in `deps update --help` pointing to `apm update --dry-run` as the safe alternative.

---

### Clean Areas

The following commands and areas passed all consistency checks:

- **Command/doc parity**: All 33 top-level CLI commands have a matching reference page under `docs/src/content/docs/reference/cli/`. No documented command is missing from the CLI; no CLI command is missing from the docs.
- **Error handling**: `apm install --nonexistent-flag`, `apm deps info` (missing arg), and `apm config set` (missing args) all produce clean, actionable error messages with usage hints -- no stack traces or crashes.
- **`--help` flag**: Works correctly on every inspected command and subcommand.
- **`--global` / `-g` flag**: Present and consistently described across all commands that support it (`install`, `uninstall`, `update`, `compile`, `deps list`, `deps tree`, `deps update`).
- **`--dry-run` flag**: Present and consistent across `install`, `uninstall`, `update`, `compile`, and `deps clean`.
- **Runtime subcommands**: `list`, `setup`, `status`, `remove` -- all documented and all functional.
- **MCP subcommands**: `list`, `search`, `show`, `install` -- all documented and consistent. Default limits match docs (`list`: 20, `search`: 10).
- **Typos / grammar**: No spelling errors found in inspected help text.
- **Deprecation notices** (content): Deprecated commands and flags consistently redirect users to the correct replacement command.
